title: Small propulsive-landing (VTVL) rockets: verified examples for ARGOS H1
units: SI (lbf and kgf quoted as published, with SI conversion)
evidence_rule: Only facts read on fetched pages; missing values marked MISSING; INFERRED = reasoned from the sources but not stated in them; DERIVED values computed from published figures; ours = estimates/SIM, not physical approval.
identity: The 'examples' and 'notes' fields below are the same content as the returned research result; the other fields are metadata.

ours.name: ARGOS H1 (engine CAD v3.5.1 in GNC reference vehicle RV-1c)
ours.status: Nothing built or flown. Engine = real CAD v3.5.1; N2O tank = concept, length ESTIMATE; airframe/fins/legs/nose/bays = ASSUMED GNC reference vehicle RV-1c (not Lauty's design); masses = current lead estimate, not frozen; flight figures = SIM.
ours.propulsion: hybrid N2O/ABS (2.0 kg N2O, 0.40 kg ABS grain), pintle throttle (throttle_frac = F/500 N), gimballed engine on two TVC servos with pushrods (BOM v3.5.1 ENG-GM-15 qty 2, ENG-GM-17 qty 2; 8 deg stop, slew >= 100 deg/s); roll RCS provision only (gnc.json roll_rcs_provision)
ours.flight_profile_SIM: full-thrust TVC ascent -> MECO -> nose-first coast -> nose drogue at apogee -> engine relight at ~57-67 m and ~22 m/s, drogue released on Pc confirmation ('no retry: a no-light is a mission loss') -> throttled TVC landing burn -> touchdown ~1 m/s on 4 deployable legs (gnc.json flight_profile.recommended_baseline.note_v3)

free_landing_summary.Scout F: YES (2022); untethered status INFERRED (no tether in either fetched source; primary video unread)
free_landing_summary.Xombie (XA-0.1B): YES (first free flight 19 Sep 2009); in-flight relight May 2010, tether status and post-relight landing of that flight MISSING
free_landing_summary.Gyroc: NOT FOUND (tethered in all published tests through 2022)
free_landing_summary.HTTP-3AT / HTTP-4: NO for HTTP-3AT (tethered, 2020); NOT FOUND for HTTP-4 (hover reported, date and tether status MISSING)

examples.name: Colibri [FREE PROPULSIVE LANDING: YES]
examples.builder: Gruyere Space Program (GSP), Swiss student association at EPFL
examples.propulsion: Liquid bipropellant N2O/IPA, in-house F-100 engine: 1.2 kN at launch; rated 1 kN, throttleable 25-125 %; gimballed ('orientable') engine guided by GNSS + INS. Not a hybrid.
examples.size_mass: 2.5 m tall, ~100 kg ('100-kilogram, 2.5-metre rocket hopper'; wet/dry basis not stated). Diameter MISSING.
examples.what_it_did: FREE PROPULSIVE LANDING: YES. First tested 2 Jun 2024; 22 low hops on a passive safety harness by 13 Aug 2024 (max 8 m); then a free-flight campaign of eight free flights over three days, the highest to 105 m with ~30 m lateral translation and return to the pad, ~60 s. The 105 m free flight was on 18 Oct 2024 (Interesting Engineering, published 22 Oct 2024). Over 50 flights in total (JAVAD); described as the first rocket hopper to fly freely in Europe. Engine operation in flight (continuous burn, or shutdown and relight): not stated in the fetched sources.
examples.comparison_to_ours: Closest published analogue found: N2O oxidiser, throttled and gimballed, 2.5 m vs our 2.03 m. But ~5.7x our liftoff mass (100 vs ~17.4 kg), 2.4x our max thrust (1.2 kN vs 500 N); DERIVED liftoff T/W ~1.2 vs our ~2.9. Liquid N2O/IPA, not hybrid. Continuous burn from take-off to touchdown: INFERRED (not stated in sources); no coast or relight is reported, so it gives no evidence on our boost-coast-drogue-relight-landing sequence. Its harnessed-hops-then-free-flight campaign is a precedent for a staged test plan.
examples.evidence_quote: "During the flight, Colibri took off and flew to an altitude of 105 meters. It then flew 30 meters southeast before returning to the launchpad and performing a successful landing." ... "The hop test took place on Friday, October 18." (Interesting Engineering, 22 Oct 2024) | "Colibri is the first rocket hopper to fly freely in Europe" (JAVAD customer story)

examples.name: Scout F [FREE PROPULSIVE LANDING: YES - untethered status INFERRED]
examples.propulsion: Hobby solid motors ('standard hobby-grade solid fuel rocket motors'; designations and count MISSING). Hackaday names a 'descent motor' and refers to 'the motors' (plural); a separate ascent motor before it is INFERRED (primary YouTube video unread). Servo-driven TVC mount (3D-printed, later machined aluminium). No throttle: thrust shaped by 'a pair of ceramic pincers which block the thrust of the motors as required'. Carbon-fibre spring legs released by nichrome wire.
examples.size_mass: MISSING (not stated on any fetched page; model-rocket scale).
examples.what_it_did: FREE PROPULSIVE LANDING: YES, untethered status INFERRED: a launched model rocket that landed on its descent motor and legs; neither fetched source mentions a tether, and the primary video was not read. Reported 2-5 Aug 2022 (The Drive 2 Aug, Hackaday 5 Aug) after seven years of attempts begun in 2015. Altitude and landing accuracy MISSING.
examples.comparison_to_ours: The only example found with a separate landing (descent) motor, i.e. a second propulsive event for the landing, as our relight is. If the INFERRED sequence (TVC ascent, unpowered coast, landing burn on deployable legs) is right, it is also the closest in mission profile to our boost-coast-relight-landing; the primary video is needed to confirm it. Differs in propulsion (unthrottleable solid motors vs our throttled hybrid relight) and scale (hobby motors; mass MISSING, so it cannot be compared with our 17.4 kg or 500 N on the evidence available).
examples.evidence_quote: "Now, 7 years into the rollercoaster journey, he has finally achieved that goal with the latest version of his Scout rocket." ... "Many things need to come together to launch AND land a rocket on standard hobby-grade solid fuel rocket motors." (Hackaday, 5 Aug 2022) | "The rocket is notable for being, by all accounts I could find, the first model rocket landed with solid rocket motors." (The Drive, 2 Aug 2022)

examples.name: Xombie (XA-0.1B) [FREE PROPULSIVE LANDING: YES]
examples.builder: Masten Space Systems (small company, Mojave, USA)
examples.propulsion: Liquid LOX/isopropyl alcohol, single regeneratively cooled engine: 750 lbf design (3.3 kN, spring 2009), over 810 lbf (3.6 kN) in Sep 2009, ~900 lbf (~4 kN) by Oct 2009 per Wikipedia. Restartable in flight (May 2010); Masten speaks of 'Combining throttle-ability and restart-ability in the same propulsion system'. Throttle range and gimbal details MISSING on fetched pages.
examples.size_mass: MISSING (no height or mass for XA-0.1B on any fetched page).
examples.what_it_did: FREE PROPULSIVE LANDING: YES. Crane-tethered hops from May 2009; first free flight 19 Sep 2009; longest flight 93 s between two pads 60 m apart, landing 'within a few inches of the target'. Qualified for the NASA Lunar Lander Challenge Level One second prize (USD 150,000) on 7 Oct 2009 with 16 cm average landing accuracy. In-flight engine relight demonstrated May 2010 (Universe Today, 26 May 2010; Masten: the first VTVL vehicle to re-light a rocket engine in flight); the propulsion and vehicle systems were engineered for a 2 s shutdown-to-restart cycle. Tether status and post-relight landing of that flight MISSING: Masten calls the ability to 'turn off our engine, reignite it in flight, successfully regain control and land' 'the next big milestone' and then writes 'With the completion of this milestone', which suggests but does not state a landing.
examples.comparison_to_ours: Small-company precedent for the crane-tether-then-free-flight path and for precision pad landings, and the only example found with an in-flight (liquid) engine relight: the step our profile cannot do without (gnc.json note_v3: 'no retry: a no-light is a mission loss'). Its in-flight off-time is not stated (systems engineered for 2 s), whereas our relight follows a ballistic coast and a drogue descent; tether status and post-relight landing of that flight MISSING. ~6.7-8x our max thrust (3.3-4.0 kN vs 500 N); mass MISSING. Cryogenic LOX/IPA liquid bipropellant, not a hybrid.
examples.evidence_quote: "The longest flight spanned 93 seconds and took place between two pads 60 meters apart" ... "We landed within a few inches of the target." (Military & Aerospace Electronics, 23 Sep 2009) | "XA-0.1B, nicknamed "Xombie", first flew free of tether 19 September 2009" ... "After seeing Masten's success with Xombie in-air relight and vertical landing, SpaceX began evaluating this technique for use on the Falcon 9 booster." (Wikipedia) | "Xombie, Masten's most-flown vehicle, carried out the test Wednesday and became the first VTVL vehicle to successfully re-light a rocket engine in flight." ... "to allow for a 2 second cycle time from shutdown to restart" (Masten press release; page undated) | "successfully demonstrated in-air engine re-light capability on their Xombie vehicle" (Universe Today, 26 May 2010)

examples.name: Gyroc [FREE PROPULSIVE LANDING: NOT FOUND - tethered in all published tests through 2022]
examples.builder: Airborne Engineering Ltd (AEL), Westcott, UK (small company)
examples.year: 2019 (first tethered test); several tethered flights in 2022
examples.propulsion: Liquid N2O/IPA ('The oxidiser is Nitrous Oxide and the fuel in Isopropyl Alcohol'), two propellant tanks. SNARK engine, ~300 N nominal thrust, 'deeply throttled (of order 5:1)' by servo-actuated propellant valves; engine on a universal joint pointed by a pair of linear actuators; no roll control ('complete control of the vehicle except in roll').
examples.size_mass: ~20 kg ('weighs about 20kg', AEL 2019 page); dry ~16 kg / wet ~25 kg (AEL 2022 paper). Height, diameter MISSING.
examples.what_it_did: FREE PROPULSIVE LANDING: NOT FOUND (tethered in all published tests through 2022). June 2019 test: took off from blocks, hovered briefly with only the attitude and altitude loops closed (no sideways control), descended and shut down, tethered to a gantry. 2022 paper: 'flown on several occasions in 2022' under a safety tether; the reported flight held position and attitude 1 m above the liftoff point for ~10 s (position within ~0.2 m), then a 'powered descent onto the tether'. A free flight without the tether is stated only as a plan. The project page's 'can hover for over 30 seconds' is a capability claim; the dated published hover is ~10 s. Later in an ESA programme.
examples.comparison_to_ours: Nearest in mass found: wet ~25 kg vs our ~17.4 kg liftoff estimate (~1.4x). Same oxidiser, throttled, and gimballed by two actuators as ours is (two TVC servos). Thrust ~300 N nominal vs our 500 N max; DERIVED liftoff T/W ~1.2 (300 N / 25 kg) vs our ~2.9. Liquid N2O/IPA, not hybrid; no roll control (ours: roll RCS provision only). Only tethered flights published: it does not demonstrate a free landing.
examples.evidence_quote: "It is tethered to a gantry to prevent damage to the vehicle in the event that it has to be shut down prematurely." (AEL news, 13 Jun 2019) | "Gyroc has a dry mass of ~16Kg and a wet mass of ~25Kg." ... "The SNARK engine has a nominal thrust of approximately 300N and can be deeply throttled (of order 5:1)." ... "Gyroc has been flown on several occasions in 2022" ... "before a powered descent onto the tether" (Moore, Greig, Waugh, Macfarlane, 'Flight testing of the Gyroc VTVL platform', AEL paper SP2022-401, Estoril, 9-13 May 2022)

examples.name: HTTP-3AT, successor HTTP-4 [FREE PROPULSIVE LANDING: NO for HTTP-3AT (tethered); NOT FOUND for HTTP-4]
examples.builder: Advanced Rocket Research Center (ARRC), Hsinchu, Taiwan: 'an autonomous sounding rocket research organization' 'established at National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University (NYCU) in 2012' (university-based)
examples.propulsion: Hybrid ('hybrid rocket boosters'). HTTP-3AT: four Sam-á-Tsiáu engines, 'same as the second stage of the HTTP-3A', with four main throttle valves and TVC actuators; 3AT propellants MISSING (the projects page lists an N2O pressure tank and an H2O2 running tank for HTTP-3A, not for the 3AT). ARRC lists 150 kgf x 4 vacuum thrust for the HTTP-3A second stage, not confirmed for the 3AT at sea level. HTTP-4: single engine gimballed by two direct-drive servo motors, a throttle valve fed by a blow-down oxidiser tank, two cold-gas vernier thrusters for roll.
examples.size_mass: MISSING (no dimensions or mass on fetched pages).
examples.what_it_did: FREE PROPULSIVE LANDING: NO for HTTP-3AT (tethered; ARRC's vocus.cc post says the T in HTTP-3AT means Tethered). 2020 tethered hover series: crash on the 3rd attempt (no explosion), first successful hover of 1 s on the 5th (ARRC post dated 20 Aug 2020), 25 s hover on the 6th (8 Sep 2020). ARRC's world-first VTVL claim (full sentence in the evidence quote) is a self-claim resting on these tethered tests, not independently verified. HTTP-4: hover with attitude and position control reported, date and tether status MISSING; VTVL flight tests are listed as a goal, landing outcome MISSING.
examples.comparison_to_ours: The only hybrid VTVL vehicles found, the same propulsion class as our N2O/ABS hybrid. The HTTP-4 architecture (single gimballed hybrid engine, two servo actuators, throttle valve, blow-down oxidiser, roll thrusters) mirrors ours most closely (ours: two TVC servos, pintle throttle, roll RCS provision only). The published record shows tethered HTTP-3AT hovers (1 s, then 25 s) after a crash, and an undated HTTP-4 hover of unknown tether status: no public free hybrid landing was found. Scale MISSING.
examples.evidence_quote: "ARRC is the first in the world to achieve vertical takeoff and vertical landing (VTVL) with hybrid rockets!" ... "The 5th HTTP-3AT tethered hovering test succeeded !" ... "We successfully hovered in air for one second." ... "Though the HTTP-3AT rocket crashed during the third test, since we implement hybrid rocket boosters, no explosion occurred." (ARRC, 20 Aug 2020) | "2020年9月8日，第6次繫留懸浮飛行測試，飛行測試25秒成功!" (8 Sep 2020, 6th tethered hover flight test, 25 s flight test successful) ... "而這支火箭名稱HTTP-3AT的T就是Tethered的意思。" (the T in the rocket name HTTP-3AT means Tethered) (ARRC post on vocus.cc) | "During hovering, we demonstrated attitude and position control capabilities." (ARRC projects page, HTTP-4)

notes:
v1.1 (2026-10-19) replaces v1.0 (2026-10-15) after an independent verification. examples.json holds these same examples and notes, plus metadata (our vehicle's figures and a free-landing summary).
1. FREE (untethered) propulsive landings verified: Colibri (2024), Masten Xombie (2009), Scout F (2022; untethered status INFERRED: no tether in either fetched source, primary video unread). Not found: AEL Gyroc (tethered in every published test through 2022), ARRC HTTP-3AT (tethered, 2020) and HTTP-4 (hover reported; date and tether status MISSING).
2. No example matches our full combination (hybrid, throttled, gimballed, boost-coast-drogue-relight-landing, free landing), but two precedents cover the critical second ignition: Xombie is the only example found with an in-flight liquid-engine relight (May 2010; tether status and post-relight landing of that flight MISSING), and Scout F is the only one with a separate landing (descent) motor (solid; its boost-coast sequence INFERRED). The only hybrid VTVL examples (ARRC) show tethered or undated hovers, no free landing. The search was not exhaustive, so no originality or superiority claim follows.
3. DERIVED from published values: liftoff thrust-to-weight Colibri ~1.2 (1.2 kN / 100 kg; mass basis unstated), Gyroc ~1.2 (300 N / 25 kg wet), ours ~2.9 (500 N / 17.4 kg lead estimate). Our values are estimates/SIM only: no physical approval.
4. Verified but excluded as out of scale (large company): Honda experimental reusable rocket, 17 Jun 2025, Taiki (Hokkaido): 6.3 m, 0.85 m diameter, 900 kg dry / 1,312 kg wet (~75x our liftoff mass), 271.4 m altitude, 56.6 s flight, landed within 37 cm of target (https://global.honda/en/topics/2025/c_2025-06-17ceng.html). The page does not state the propellants or explicitly say 'untethered'.
5. Checked, NOT counted (no flight or landing found): Purdue PSP TADPOLE, a throttleable regeneratively cooled bipropellant liquid engine, hot fire only; it 'won $15,000 for the Throttle Milestone' of the Collegiate Propulsive Lander Challenge, and a 'powered 160 foot hop' is a stated future goal (https://engineering.purdue.edu/AAE/spotlights/2026/PSP-tadpoles, last modified 25 Mar 2026). Also checked in v1.0, no flight or landing found (source URLs not recorded, so their details were dropped): Space Team Aachen Hopper, TUM ASCENT hopper, UConn AIAA Propulsive Landing, Konkuk University hybrid VTVL, IIT Madras hybrid soft landing. Copenhagen Suborbitals: no propulsive-landing vehicle found in one search; not included.
6. Sources not readable: the BPS.space YouTube video page (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SH3lR2GLgT0) was refused by the WebFetch proxy with HTTP 429 in v1.0 (not retried); the Vice article on Scout F was blocked by robots.txt. So Scout F rests on secondary press (Hackaday, The Drive): its motor sequence and tether status are INFERRED, its size, mass and motor designations MISSING.
7. Verification method: shell downloads were refused by the proxy (403 CONNECT) in v1.0 and again in v1.1, so quotes were checked by WebFetch exact-string queries on the extracted page text, not against raw HTML (the full-width commas of the vocus.cc quote were confirmed this way). The Scout F Drive quote drops the italics on 'solid'.
8. Source spread: Masten thrust differs by date and source: 750 lbf design, >810 lbf (Sep 2009), ~900 lbf (Wikipedia, Oct 2009). Colibri: 1.2 kN at launch (press) vs 1 kN rated, 25-125 % (JAVAD); over 50 flights (JAVAD).
9. Contradiction preserved: the brief's first-flight target apogee is 210 m (SIM), while gnc.json flight_profile gives 'A1 MECO on predicted apogee 285 m' (rev2.1). Not reconciled here.
10. Carried from the brief, not researched here: the GNC v3d tank at z 0.55-0.995 m clashes with the v3.5.1 engine top at z 0.558 m. The tank moves to z 0.58-1.08 m (tank-line route TO-DEFINE), and avionics, battery and backup chute shift forward (they still fit in the 1.70 m tube).
11. Verifier issues in v1.1: (a) MAJOR, Xombie relight: FIXED. 'no coast/relight' is replaced by the May 2010 relight with tether status and post-relight landing MISSING; Universe Today and the Masten press release were fetched and cited; the Wikipedia sentence is quoted; 'The hoppers burn continuously' is deleted; note 2 names both precedents. Wording kept to the sources: they say the systems were engineered 'to allow for a 2 second cycle time from shutdown to restart', not that the in-flight gap was 2 s. (b) Gyroc: FIXED from the AEL 2022 paper (~300 N; dry ~16 / wet ~25 kg; tethered ~10 s hover at 1 m in 2022; T/W ~1.2; label NOT FOUND). (c) Colibri continuous burn: FIXED, labelled INFERRED (not stated in sources) and no longer used in the notes. (d) Colibri date: FIXED (105 m free flight on 18 Oct 2024; article published 22 Oct 2024; both re-read). (e) Scout F: FIXED (ascent-coast-descent sequence and untethered status labelled INFERRED; date 2-5 Aug 2022). (f) ARRC: FIXED (exact sentences re-read with full-width punctuation kept; vocus.cc and arrc.tw/about added; HTTP-4 hover added; HTTP-3A tank note added). NOT FIXED: the HTTP-4 '100-100 VTVL hopping flight' goal, because two fetches of arrc.tw/projects found neither '100-100' nor 'hop' in the extracted text. (g) Unsourced numbers in the notes: FIXED (Technology Review ~850 lbf and Kistler 53 flights dropped; excluded vehicles reduced to names, except Purdue, which was re-read and now carries its URL). (h) File vs output: FIXED (examples.json regenerated as v1.1 from the same content). Two wording corrections beyond the list: Xombie 'won' the LLC prize became 'qualified for' (Wikipedia's wording), and the ARRC 1 s hover date is given as the post date.
